key_insight: SIM-PINN combines projection-based equation splitting, iterative coupling, and multi-stage neural networks to address convergence and accuracy challenges in incompressible flow simulation.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a mesh-free approach to incompressible flow prediction while reducing optimization difficulties caused by nonlinear dynamics and coupled velocity–pressure constraints.
method: Split Navier–Stokes into linearized momentum and pressure Poisson equations, solved with separate neural networks.
Couple the solutions through projection-based inner iterations to recover the nonlinear system upon convergence.
Use successive momentum-network stages to refine velocity fields at targeted frequencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved convergence and accuracy in steady lid-driven cavity and unsteady Kolmogorov flow simulations, without quantitative metrics.
watch_item: Training cost and robustness of the iterative, multi-network workflow for more complex flows remain unclear from the abstract.
paper_title: Projection-based segregated, iterative, and multi-stage physics-informed neural network for incompressible Navier-stokes equations
